Title: Diagnosis of test `testLinearCombinationWithSingleElementArray`

Details:
The test `testLinearCombinationWithSingleElementArray` checks the outcome of the method `MathArrays.linearCombination(double[], double[])` for the specific case where both arrays `a` and `b` have a single element each. The expected value is the simple product of the single elements `a[0] * b[0]`.

Examining the code of `MathArrays.linearCombination(double[], double[])`, we observe the following:
- It first checks if the lengths of input arrays `a` and `b` match.
- It initializes an array `prodHigh` and a sum accumulator `prodLowSum`.
- A loop runs through each element of the arrays, calculating high-precision multiplication components for each pair `(a[i], b[i])` and storing the high part of the product in `prodHigh[i]` and accumulating corrections in `prodLowSum`.
- After the loop, it attempts to accurately sum up the `prodHigh` components using a compensated summation approach, using variable names `sHighPrev`, `sPrime`, and `sLowSum`.
- The summation logic for `prodHigh` assumes at least two elements in the arrays, because it accesses `prodHigh[1]` unconditionally.
- Finally, the summation results (`prodLowSum` and `sLowSum`) are combined with the high sum to produce the final result.

The fault arises because in the case where `len == 1`, `prodHigh[1]` does not exist and accessing `prodHigh[1]` results in an `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` or misbehaviour. The summation logic is not guarded for the single-element case.

The likely intended fix would be to handle the case `len == 1` as a simple multiplication directly, returning `prodHigh[0] + prodLowSum`, or otherwise modifying the summation logic to correctly handle the scenario with a single-element array gracefully.

This bug causes the failure of `testLinearCombinationWithSingleElementArray` which expected a valid multiplication output but instead encounters the internal access error due to the assumption that the input arrays have at least two elements.

Recommended fix locations:

- `org.apache.commons.math3.util.MathArrays.linearCombination(double[], double[])`

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
